note: All three examples use кружок in the 'hobby club / study group' sense, which the headword gloss 'circle' does not cover — the English is right, so it is the gloss that likely needs widening.

en_alt: The plane turned onto its right wing.
note: 'Banked' is a fair idiomatic reading of поверну́л на крыло́; the literal turn-verb rendering is worth accepting too.

en_alt: The bird's wing is broken.
note: The short-participle construction also reads naturally as a possessive subject.

ru: Он стоя́л на крыльце́ и ждал госте́й.
en: He stood on the porch and waited for guests.
note: The Russian coordinates two finite verbs with и; the participial 'waiting for' hides the conjunction the sentence is teaching.

en_alt: Snow lay on the porch.
note: The literal lie-verb rendering is natural English and should be accepted by the drill.

en_alt: Snow lies on the roof.
note: Literal rendering of лежи́т is natural English and equally valid.

en: There are different lids in the box.
note: я́щик is glossed 'box' corpus-wide and nothing in the sentence marks it as a drawer, so the tap-hint contradicts the translation.

en_alt: Cover the saucepan with the lid.
note: кастрю́ля is glossed 'saucepan'; accept that wording alongside 'pot'.

en_alt: The jar's lid has been lost.
note: Equally valid rendering of the reflexive потеря́лась.

en_alt: The children were building a tower out of cubes.
note: стро́или is imperfective — the process reading should also be accepted, since a completed build would be постро́или.

en_alt: The girl is playing with a doll.
note: Russian present covers both English present forms.

en_alt: He is studying Russian culture.
note: Russian present covers both English present forms.

en_alt: The church's dome shines with gold.
note: Equally valid word order and a closer match to the gloss 'to shine'.

en: Pigeons were flying under the dome.
note: лета́ли is the multidirectional imperfective — flying about, not a single passage; 'flew under the dome' reads as one directional flight (пролете́ли).

en: The hen was roasted for lunch.
note: обе́д is glossed 'lunch' corpus-wide; 'dinner' reads as the evening meal in en_gb and contradicts the tap-hint.
Here курс is the exchange rate, a sense the headword gloss 'course' does not cover; the English is correct, so the gloss is the half that may need widening.

ru: Он записа́лся на курс ру́сского языка́.
en_alt: He signed up for a Russian language course.
note: записа́ться is 'sign up' as well as 'enrol'; both should be accepted.

ru: В ма́леньких ку́хнях тру́дно размести́ть большу́ю семью́.
en_alt: In small kitchens it is difficult to accommodate a large family.
note: Closer to the glosses of тру́дно and размести́ть, and equally natural.
сде́лать ремо́нт is a fixed expression; 'renovated' is the right idiomatic rendering.

en: There is a delicious smell from the kitchen.
note: English does not call a smell 'tasty'; вку́сно is glossed 'deliciously' and 'delicious' is what a native speaker writes here.

en_alt: The children were jumping into a heap of leaves.
note: пры́гали is imperfective and repeated; the progressive reading should also be accepted.

en_alt: They carry out experiments in the laboratory.
note: The impersonal third-plural also renders naturally as an active 'they' clause.

ru: Мы се́ли на ла́вку у подъе́зда.

en_alt: There are wooden benches in the garden.
note: The existential rendering of стоя́т is equally valid English.

ru: Де́ти пое́хали в ла́герь на ле́то.

en_alt: He was holding the coin in his palm.
note: держа́л is imperfective; the progressive reading is equally valid.

en_alt: Snowflakes were melting on his palms.
note: та́яли is imperfective; the progressive reading fits the scene at least as well.

en_alt: The lamp stands on the table.
note: The literal posture verb is natural English and is what стои́т teaches.

en_alt: The light bulb has burned out.
note: Equally standard rendering of перегоре́ть.

en_alt: He picked a bouquet of lilies of the valley.
note: буке́т is glossed 'bouquet'; accept that wording alongside 'bunch'.

en_alt: I cooked delicious noodles.
note: пригото́вить is glossed 'to prepare; to cook'; both renderings should be accepted.

en: A white swan was swimming on the lake.
note: «по о́зеру» is movement over the lake's surface, not «че́рез» = across, and imperfective плыл is a process rather than a completed crossing.

en_alt: The lion is the king of beasts.
note: The article-less set phrase is the commoner English form and should be accepted.

ru: В зоопа́рке львам даю́т мя́со по утра́м.
Об э́тих гора́х есть мно́го леге́нд.
Об э́том о́зере есть ста́рая леге́нда.

en_alt: Smoking is harmful to the lungs.
note: вре́дный is glossed 'harmful'; the literal rendering is natural English.
Singular лёгкое is unusual medically but matches the singular headword the sentence is teaching.

en_alt: The river became covered with ice.
note: покры́лась is a change of state, which the inchoative rendering shows more clearly.

en_alt: He watered the flowers with the watering can.
note: 'With the watering can' is the more idiomatic English for из ле́йки; keep the literal 'from' as the shown form.

As written, nominative Прика́з is the subject of active отда́л, so the sentence says 'the order gave to the lieutenant'; the impersonal third-plural о́тдали gives exactly the existing English passive.

ru: Принима́йте э́то лека́рство два ра́за в день.

en_alt: The professor is delivering a lecture.
note: чита́ть ле́кцию is a fixed collocation; 'delivering' is an equally standard rendering.

en_alt: The students were listening to the lecture.
note: слу́шали is imperfective; the progressive reading is equally valid.

en_alt: The train goes as far as Leningrad.
note: до marks the terminus, which 'as far as' shows and plain 'to' does not.

en_alt: Clouds floated over Leningrad.
note: плы́ли is the float/sail verb; accept the literal rendering alongside 'drifted'.

en: The present is tied with a red ribbon.
note: переви́т is 'bound/twined round', not 'wrapped' (обёрнут) — 'wrapped with a ribbon' suggests wrapping paper rather than a ribbon tied around the parcel.

ru: В со́сновых леса́х ле́том полно́ я́год.
Мы пошли́ в лес за гриба́ми.
en_alt: We went into the forest for mushrooms.
note: в + accusative is motion into; both prepositions are natural here.

en_alt: Dense forests are visible beyond the river.
note: видны́ is glossed 'visible'; the adjectival rendering tracks the Russian more closely.

ru: По со́сновым леса́м раски́даны ти́хие озёра.

en_alt: I am waiting impatiently for summer.
note: с нетерпе́нием is literally 'with impatience'; the literal reading teaches the instrumental phrase.

ru: В нача́ле ле́та мы е́здим на да́чу.

note: Directional accusative after посади́ть is defensible ('brought the plane down into the fog'), though в тума́не would be the commoner phrasing.

ru: По́сле лече́ния он почу́вствовал себя́ лу́чше.

en_alt: He needs money for the treatment.
note: Russian has no articles; both determiner choices are valid here.
ве́рить + dative is 'trust/have faith in', so 'trust' is right despite the gloss 'to believe'.

en_alt: The party leader made a speech.
note: Equally standard English collocation.

en_alt: The leaders of two countries met.
note: Russian has no articles; the bare-plural reading is equally valid.

en_alt: The pupil rubbed out the crooked lines.
note: 'Rubbed out' is the everyday en_gb rendering of стёр.

ru: Он написа́л письмо́ на одно́м листе́.
en_alt: He wrote the letter on a single sheet.
note: одно́м here carries the 'a single' sense; both renderings are valid.

en_alt: She covered many sheets with writing.
note: Equally natural rendering of исписа́ть.
For paper, чи́стый is 'blank'; 'a clean sheet' reads in en_gb as the football/fresh-start idiom rather than an unused sheet of paper.
All three examples use листо́к in the 'small sheet of paper' sense, which the headword gloss 'leaf' does not cover; the English is right, so the gloss is what likely needs widening.

en_alt: A small sheet is lying on the table.
note: The progressive reading of лежи́т is at least as natural in English.

en_alt: Write down the address on the sheet.
note: записа́ть is 'write down'; the prefix is worth showing.

ru: Маши́не ну́жно ещё де́сять ли́тров бензи́на.
